choices.text: Queen studio; 4.3 guest rating; pool and hot tub; $218 total; a 5-minute covered walk to the course building.
King studio; 4.6 guest rating; pool and hot tub; $218 total; an 11-minute covered walk to the course building.
Queen studio; 4.7 guest rating; no pool or hot tub; $212 total; a 6-minute covered walk to the course building.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: the query alone leaves a legitimate tradeoff among rating, bed type, amenity completeness, price, and walking distance. History is needed to know that a 4.3 rating is sufficient, that the full recovery bundle matters, and that queen is Kara's default for this scoped one-bed room rather than king being an automatic improvement.
probes.gold_action: Hold the queen studio in A as the lead option.
probes.label_rationale: A preserves Kara's recurring queen default for a solo one-bed teaching stay while still clearing her normal customer-rating floor and providing the full pool, hot-tub, and fitness bundle. B's stronger rating is a real competing benefit, but higher ratings above the 4.0 floor are a bonus rather than a hard 4.5-plus rule; it also gives up the queen and adds a modest walk. C keeps the queen but gives up two preferred recovery amenities. This is not a rule against king rooms: it is a choice of the established queen default when the competing quality differences are non-mandatory.
probes.query: Kara needs one refundable room for a three-night solo pediatric skills-course stay. She will have late teaching days, no separate-bed arrangement is requested, and all three options have confirmed in-room coffee, a mini-fridge, fitness access, the same cancellation terms, and rates within reimbursement. Ratings below use the same guest-review source and each has more than 800 reviews. Which room should be the lead hold?

choices.text: Trail lodge queen room; 4.5 guest rating; fitness room but no pool or hot tub; $248 total; 4 minutes from the trail-shuttle pickup.
Resort king room; 4.4 guest rating; pool, hot tub, and fitness room; $254 total; 12 minutes from the trail-shuttle pickup.
Spa-inn queen room; 4.6 guest rating; pool and fitness room but no hot tub; $251 total; 6 minutes from the trail-shuttle pickup.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: no option is generically dominant. The query requires balancing a queen, slightly better rating, lower price, and trail proximity against a confirmed king and a complete recovery bundle. The history is needed both to apply the active-recovery amenity preference and to recognize that queen is a default, not a prohibition on a specifically offered king.
probes.gold_action: Lead with the resort's confirmed king room and its complete recovery-amenity bundle.
probes.label_rationale: For this active recovery weekend, the resort supplies Kara's full preferred pool, hot-tub, and fitness bundle. Its confirmed king is an expressly available, acceptable one-bed arrangement for Kara and her partner; the history does not support rejecting every king in favor of a queen. The small rate and shuttle-distance differences, along with C's higher rating and queen, make C a credible alternative, but neither A nor C has the complete recovery bundle.
probes.query: Kara and her partner need one refundable room for a two-night hike-and-race recovery weekend. They want one shared bed, not separate beds. Every option has confirmed in-room coffee and a mini-fridge, uses the same review source, and has the same cancellation deadline. Which room should lead the shortlist?

choices.text: Campus hotel, 4.6 guest rating, $210 total, 2-minute indoor walk, and fitness access. The reservation is run-of-house: it records “queen requested,” but the actual room may be a queen, a king, or two doubles at check-in.
Suite hotel, 4.2 guest rating, $204 total, 9-minute covered walk, and fitness access. A king studio is confirmed on the reservation.
Nearby hotel, 4.5 guest rating, $204 total, 6-minute covered walk, but no fitness access. A queen studio is confirmed on the reservation.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: A offers the best access and rating but uncertain bedding, C offers the preferred confirmed queen plus better access and rating but lacks fitness, and B offers a confirmed king plus the full recovery bundle. The query alone supplies no universal ordering of those tradeoffs; resolving it requires Kara's history on confirmed bed setups, queen as a default rather than an absolute rule, and recovery amenities after teaching days.
probes.gold_action: Hold B: the confirmed king studio with the complete recovery bundle.
probes.label_rationale: A does not provide a confirmed single larger bed and could result in the repeatedly disfavored two-double setup; a queen request is not equivalent to an actual bed confirmation. C confirms the usual queen but omits fitness, while B confirms an acceptable one-bed configuration and provides the complete pool, hot-tub, and fitness bundle for long teaching days. Selecting B applies the confirmation boundary and the king exception; it does not turn king into a general upgrade preference.
probes.query: For a three-night solo hospital teaching visit with two 7:30 a.m. starts, Kara must place one refundable hotel hold tonight; the hotels cannot provide further clarification before the cutoff. She expects to use recovery facilities after long teaching days. All listed ratings use the same guest-review source, and all options have confirmed in-room coffee, a mini-fridge, a pool, and a hot tub. No separate-bed setup is requested. Which hold should lead?
